title: Chat stream: tie-sort 500 + reload watcher + SIGTERM swallow (all fixed)
body:
Symptom: chat UI showed 1 tok/s, Very slow, 2 errs.

DONE (commits 70b021b6a, 3b605d205, 1a94a3e14):

A) context_core.py:275 scored.sort(reverse=True) on (score, episode_dict); tie compared dicts -> TypeError -> 500 on /chat/stream from turn 2 of any session -> zero streamed tokens. Fix: sort(key=lambda item: item[0]). Verified live on :8000 - turn 1 AND turn 2 both stream to status=complete.

B) main.py imported domain.shared.find_repo_root before sys.path ready -> needed PYTHONPATH=.. Fixed with inline _bootstrap_repo_root().

C) reload_includes/reload_excludes used dir/** globs; uvicorn resolve_reload_patterns globs each (node_modules/** = 40,893 entries) then runs O(n^2) Path.parents -> Config() >60s -> never binds, 100% CPU. Replaced with reload_dirs=[apps/api/server, domain, packages/core-py/domains] -> ~1ms, 1,067 files vs 29,507. CAUTION: 70b021b6a's message described this but only the bootstrap hunk landed; caught only by verifying git show HEAD afterwards.

D) pugqeep Engine.__init__ installed a process-global SIGTERM/SIGINT handler whose body was only self._running=False; self.stop() and never exited. uvicorn --reload sent SIGTERM to the child then blocked forever in Process.join() -> reload fired ONCE then wedged (parent wchan=do_wait), and plain kill <pid> needed SIGKILL. Fix: _handle_signal delegates to the handler it replaced; if none and frame is not None (real delivery, not a direct test call) restore SIG_DFL and re-raise. install_signal_handlers() made idempotent so a 2nd install no longer overwrote _old_signal_handlers with our own handler. Verified on :8003 - binds 18s, 3 reloads each respawn the child (4 procs), SIGTERM then shuts down cleanly, no SIGKILL.

E) M-blind int8 GEMM threading (matmul_int8.c). Two defects:
   1. Thread gate compared N*K (B bytes) vs 6MB - M never entered, so a 601-token prefill of a 0.8MB block took the serial branch while the single-token decode of that same block (identical N*K) was eligible. Gate now tests M*N*K MACs vs the same 6e6 (numerically identical at M=1, so the decode measurements behind the constant still hold).
   2. _gemm_threads() returned 1 unconditionally. Its rationale was measured on DECODE (M=1): warm weights already near DRAM bandwidth, hyperthreads add memory-controller contention, chip throttles (124-130ms bimodal vs stable 54-67ms serial). That never applied to prefill - B is reused across all M rows so it stays cache-resident (no DRAM contention) and the work is M times larger so spawn cost is negligible. Now _gemm_threads(M): M<=1 serial (bit-for-bit the old condition), M>1 online CPUs capped at 8. MAN_GEMM_THREADS still overrides either way.
   Results (scripts/benchmark_gemm_threading.py, Qwen2.5-0.5B shapes, M in 1/64/256/601/1024 x threads 1/4/8/default):
   - prefill 1.7-3.7x at M>=64, best rows 3.2-3.4x
   - decode (M=1) unchanged: default matches serial exactly (incl. lm_head 12.36ms serial vs 6.79ms if threaded)
   - output bit-identical at every shape, M and thread count (25/25 rows)
   End-to-end chat A/B (MAN_GEMM_THREADS=1 vs unset, 3 requests each): TTFT median 18451ms -> 9720ms (1.90x), min 15847ms -> 8738ms (1.81x), decode tok/s median 4.51 -> 10.70 (no regression). Context pipeline only 145-286ms of that, so the gain is model prefill.
   Open: prefill is only ~50% this kernel (numpy attention does not run through it), which is why end-to-end is 1.9x not 3x. Trimming the 248-tok system_extra (personality 103 + style 74 + task 71) would cut prefill ~46% and is the next lever.

MEASURED, not bugs: prompt = 283 tok (base 35 + system_extra 248). Prefill 46 tok/s @250 tok, 40 @500, 29 @1000, 21 @2000. AVX-512 absent is hardware (i5-9300H, 0 zmm in .so), not a build bug.

title: Frontend stops re-firing inference: no retry amplification, no immortal startup polls
body:
PROBLEM (measured, not guessed)
The frontend fires redundant inference requests of its own accord, adding load and lag on top of an already-slow backend.

A. Retry amplification on non-idempotent inference POSTs
- apps/web/lib/http-client.ts:165 DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000
- apps/web/lib/http-client.ts:163 MAX_RETRIES = 2  -> up to 3 attempts
- apps/web/lib/http-client.ts:756 catch block retries on TIMEOUT with NO method check
- apps/web/lib/http-client.ts:546 client aborts at 30s; the BACKEND generation is NOT cancelled
- Logged durations routinely exceed 30s (46s, 54s, 70s, 115s, 136s observed via /benchmark/responses)
Result: one user action -> up to 3 concurrent generations contending for the GIL -> each slower
-> more timeouts -> more retries. Positive feedback loop the frontend creates itself.
Exposed apiPost callers: /companion/chat, /learn/train, /learn/evaluate, /knowledge/train-adapter,
/self-train/start, /benchmark/run, /workflow/start, /memory/consolidate, /user-adapters/aggregate-best.
Note /learn/train is called from features/chat/hooks/useChatContextValue.ts:46 (inside chat).
SSE path is CORRECT (http-client.ts:1292-1300 abort -> error, no retry; only 503 retries) - do not touch.

B. Startup polls that never stop
- apps/web/app/(app)/page.tsx:252  GET /health/startup-progress every 3s FOREVER, no phase==='ready' guard (~20 req/min indefinitely)
- apps/web/app/(app)/developer/page.tsx:817,831  /health/startup-progress + /health/startup-history every 2s forever, via RAW fetch()
  -> also violates the http-client.ts single-source-of-truth rule from AGENTS.md

INVARIANT
Retry is only safe when the operation is idempotent AND the server-side effect was cancelled.
Current code gives at-least-once semantics to a side-effecting, expensive, non-idempotent operation.

PLAN
1. http-client.ts: add isIdempotent(method); gate the timeout branch (L756) and status branch (L659) on it;
   add RequestOptions.retryOnTimeout for explicit opt-in.
2. Inference POSTs pass timeout: 120_000 + retryOnTimeout: false.
3. app/(app)/page.tsx: clear interval when phase === 'ready'.
4. developer/page.tsx: raw fetch() -> apiGet, stop polling at ready.
5. TDD: timeout on POST does not retry; timeout on GET does; 503 on GET retries; startup poll stops at ready.

SCOPE GUARD (must NOT break)
- Keep retries for GET on 502/503/504/connection-refused: uvicorn --reload now works, so restarts are more frequent and that path is load-bearing.
- Do NOT touch the SSE streaming path (already correct).
- Do NOT touch DOCSTORE_* constants (documented 400-retry exception, http-client.ts:167-171).
- Startup polls must still work during actual startup; only stop once ready.

OUT OF SCOPE (open question, not approved)
- streamSse (http-client.ts:1288) has NO timeout, only the caller signal -> chat can hang indefinitely if the backend never responds. Hang-guard proposed but NOT included in this card.

SHARED WORKSPACE

- shared copy reused: reuse root node_modules + .venv, no installs

  This work goes on fix/http-retry-amplification, commits ONLY its own paths (git commit -m ... -- <paths>),
  then switches back so the other session's branch is undisturbed.

title: Truthful tok/s — decode vs end-to-end, and un-break /benchmark/metrics
body:
PROBLEM (measured, not guessed)
The web UI reports ~2 tok/s and treats it as "the benchmark and the max", even though decode was measured at 10.7 tok/s after the M-aware GEMM fix.

A. /benchmark/metrics returns 500 (E_SERIALIZATION)
- apps/api/server/routers/benchmark.py:157  getattr(provider, "num_parameters", None)
- num_parameters is a plain `def` (abstractmethod, NOT @property) — models.py:82-85, slonet_provider.py:1474
- getattr returns a BOUND METHOD -> not JSON-serializable -> whole endpoint 500s after 3 consecutive failures.

B. The Tokens/s formula measures IDLE time, not generation
- benchmark.py:138-147
    inference_time = time.time() - ctrl._last_inference_time   <-- IDLE seconds since last inference
    tokens_per_sec = total_tokens / (inference_time * total_inferences)
- decays toward 0 the longer the server sits idle.

C. The headline rate is end-to-end but labelled as throughput
- inference.py:2042  start_time set BEFORE context/RAG/prefill
- inference.py:871   duration_ms = now - start_time
- inference.py:942   record_inference(tokens, elapsed_ms=duration_ms)
- server_state.py:293-310  get_tokens_per_second() = sum(tokens)/sum(elapsed_ms)
  numerator = decode tokens only, denominator = prefill + decode + session I/O -> systematically low.
- Feeds dashboard home, StatusBar, monitoring, DebugOverlay and health_flow._check_throughput
  (>=30 Fast, >=10 OK, >=5 Slow, else Very slow).

D. The history card "Best Throughput"
- apps/web/app/(app)/benchmark/page.tsx:121 history(20); :225-228 throughput = tokens_generated / duration_ms
- BenchmarkHistoryCard.tsx:78 bestThroughput = Math.max(...) ; :141 label "Best Throughput"
- Same prefill-inclusive duration. Across all 213 logged responses the max is 12.48; true decode = 10.7.

INVARIANT
A rate named "tok/s" must have a numerator and denominator drawn from the SAME window.
Today the numerator is decode-only and the denominator is end-to-end. Two different windows = a number that means nothing.

PLAN
1. benchmark.py:157 — call num_parameters() when callable. Kills the 500.
2. benchmark.py:138-147 — replace the idle-time formula with server_state's real decode rate.
3. inference.py — record first-token and last-token timestamps in the chat stream loop (2477-2743)

60 children of the pytest process spawned by a leaked pugqeep engine each got
the parent cmdline (fork preserves argv) and ALL deadlocked in futex_do_wait —
fork-into-multithreaded-pytest reproduced at scale, exactly the hazard this
card removes (fork -> forkserver). Batch pattern: every 180s, 1-7 per batch,
20:11->21:08; main thread then blocked 9h in waitpid at exit. Also worth
noting SubprocessProcess.monitor() still waits with no timeout.

title: Session compaction prompt override: tighter, workflow-aware summary (no Relevant Files)
body:
Stock OpenCode compaction template is wordy: 6 sections, mandatory '(none)' scaffolding, plus a 'Relevant Files' inventory.

Added .opencode/plugins/compaction-tight.ts using the experimental.session.compacting hook (full prompt replacement, fail-open) with our SOP fields: Card / Branch / Journey / Gates, max 4 one-line bullets per section, no file-inventory section.

Mechanism notes: setting output.prompt replaces the built-in prompt wholesale (context only appends, so it cannot drop a section). A prompt override also suppresses OpenCode's built-in <prior-summary> embedding, so the plugin fetches the last completed compaction itself via client.message.list({order:desc}) so a second compaction still rolls forward. Hook callbacks are awaited by Plugin.trigger, so async is safe; any error leaves prompt unset and the stock prompt runs.

Typecheck: tsc --strict clean on the new file (existing plugins still show the pre-existing TS1360 satisfies-Plugin mismatch).

## Verification 2026-10-02 08:20 — live, isolated `opencode serve` (127.0.0.1:45777)

**Correction to the mechanism note above:** the prior-summary lookup does NOT use `client.message.list({order:desc})` — there is no `client.message` namespace. The plugin factory client is namespaced (`session`, `config`, `tool`, `path`, `vcs`, ...), so the call is `client.session.messages({path:{id: sessionID}, query:{limit: 10000}})` → `{data:[{info, parts}]}`; `order` is not on the SDK query type, so the plugin sorts by `info.time.created` itself. This was the real root cause of the first live run: the hook fired (`hasClient=true`) but the guard bailed silently and the **stock** template came out.

Live proof — two consecutive `POST /session/:id/summarize` (free model `opencode/mimo-v2.6-flash-free`):

- compaction #2 → log `prompt override applied (messages=6, prior-summary=yes)` — the `<prior-summary>` + merge-rules block rolled forward (a prompt override suppresses the built-in embedding, so this proves our own fetch works).
- Server log: `(messages=4, prior-summary=no)` then `(messages=6, prior-summary=yes)`.
